title: kith-jmap: role-check-before-handler-lookup order is correct security design
description: dispatch_one checks METHOD_ROLES first (role-required check) before looking up the handler map (line 412-424). This means a peer calling an owner method gets 'forbidden' not 'unknownMethod', even if no handler is registered. A contributor might suggest merging the maps to simplify dispatch, but that would allow role-checking to be bypassed if a method is registered in the wrong map. The two-map structure (handlers vs peer_handlers) enforces the typed identity contract at compile time: peer handlers receive Identity as a typed parameter, owner handlers do not need it. This prevents accidentally calling a peer method handler without verifying identity.
